```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(catcheR); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)

## Folder layout -------------------------------------------------------------
##   analysis_EB_10X/
##     scratch/   <- every input listed below
##     Output/    <- everything this document writes
SCRATCH <- file.path(params$analysis_dir, params$scratch)
OUT     <- file.path(params$analysis_dir, params$output)
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
show <- function(f, ext = "jpg") {
  p <- file.path(OUT, paste0(f, ".", ext))
  if (file.exists(p)) knitr::include_graphics(p) else invisible(NULL)
}
MAXR <- if (is.null(params$max_reads)) Inf else as.numeric(params$max_reads)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 9))
```

# The pipeline, and where this document sits in it

Four steps, in this order. Each one consumes what the previous produced, and
nothing here re-reads the FASTQ after the first step.

| # | step | reads | produces | needed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `catcheR_tenxcatch()` | the FASTQ pair, the barcode-to-gene CSVs and the called-cell list (which doubles as the correction whitelist) | the `parsecatch` object (`.rds`), `complete_table_fin`, the 13 catcheR plots and the QC panels | every step below |
| 2 | `catcheR_tenx_filtercatch()` | the object from 1 | `ValidCell` at the chosen thresholds, `cells_with_at_least_1_UCI.csv`, `new_cell_names.csv` | steps 3 and 4 |
| 3 | `catcheR_tenx_nocatch()` | the object from 1 **and** the filter from 2 | the empty-vector cells, i.e. the unperturbed control set | step 4 (optional) |
| 4 | `catcheR_tenx_seurat()` | the filter from 2, the empty set from 3, and Cell Ranger's `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5`, or the MatrixMarket triple | the Seurat object with `catcheR_status` on every cell | your downstream analysis |

**Why the order matters.** Step 3 needs step 2 because an "empty" cell is
defined as one that is *not* in the called set: without the filter there is
nothing to subtract from. Step 4 needs step 2 for the same reason and step 3
only if you want the controls labelled rather than left as `not_detected`.

**What can be repeated cheaply.** Steps 2 to 4 all act on the object, so
re-filtering at new thresholds costs seconds and never re-streams the reads.
Only step 1 is expensive.

## Where the files go

```
analysis_EB_10X/
  scratch/                       <- inputs, plus the handoff copies below
  Output/
    tenxcatch/                 <- step 1: this chemistry's own folder
      filtercatch_p15_u1_r2_f20/ <- step 2, tagged with its thresholds
```

Step 1 nests under the chemistry name so that running the Parse or PIPseq
pipeline into the same `Output/` cannot overwrite these files - the 13 plots
carrying catcheR's own names have no chemistry in the filename. Step 2 adds a
folder named for its thresholds, so a second attempt at different values sits
beside the first instead of replacing it.

Three files are *inputs to a later step* rather than deliverables:
`cells_with_at_least_1_UCI.csv`, `new_cell_names.csv` and
`complete_table_fin_<sample>.csv`. With `to_scratch: true` they are copied into
`scratch/` as `<name>_tenxcatch_<sample>.csv`, so two pipelines can
share one scratch without colliding. The originals stay in `Output/`.

## One trap in the thresholds

`UMI.count` and `percentage` exclude with a strict `>`, `min.cell.UMI` includes
with `>=`. So `UMI.count = 1` keeps pairs of **two or more** UMIs, a UCI at
exactly 15% does **not** pass `percentage = 15`, and a cell with exactly 20
cassette UMIs **does** pass `min.cell.UMI = 20`. The floor keeps
applying by default: step 2 also defaults it to 20, so it stays in force unless
you pass another value (`0` disables it). This document passes it explicitly at
both steps, so the YAML header is the single source of truth.

# What this document does

`catcheR_tenxcatch()` is the native R entry point for 10x Genomics barcode
enrichment libraries. It replaces the original `catcheR_10Xcatch()`, which
drove bundled shell scripts through `system()` and wrote its intermediates
into the input folder; this one streams the FASTQ in R, writes only into
`Output/`, and shares its whole downstream half with the PIPseq and Parse
entry points.

Everything is built from the parameters in the header, so running another
sample means changing `sample_name` and the FASTQ names — nothing in the body
needs editing.

# Inputs

```{r inputs}
need <- c(params$fastq_r1, params$fastq_r2, params$barcodes_genes,
          params$cell_whitelist)
inv <- data.frame(
  file    = need,
  role    = c("read 1 - cell barcode + UMI", "read 2 - cassette",
              rep("barcode-to-gene reference", length(params$barcodes_genes)),
              "Cell Ranger called cells"),
  exists  = file.exists(file.path(SCRATCH, need)),
  size_MB = round(file.size(file.path(SCRATCH, need)) / 1024^2, 1))
stopifnot(all(inv$exists))
kable(inv, caption = sprintf("Inputs found in %s", SCRATCH))
```

The cell list can be given three ways, and the same file serves as both the
error-correction whitelist and the called-cell denominator:

| source | how to pass it |
|---|---|
| `barcodes.tsv.gz` from `filtered_feature_bc_matrix/` | `cell.whitelist = "barcodes.tsv.gz"` |
| a plain text file, one barcode per line | as above (this template's default) |
| `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` | same argument; needs the `hdf5r` package |

Suffixes like `-1` are stripped on read, so either form works.

# Extraction and first-stage QC

One pass over the read pair. This is the only expensive step — roughly 15
minutes for a 28 M pair library — so the chunk is cached: re-knitting to adjust
a plot or a threshold does not re-read the FASTQ. Set `max_reads` in the header
to a few million for a dry run.

```{r tenxcatch, cache=TRUE}
res <- catcheR_tenxcatch(
  folder            = SCRATCH,
  fastq.read1       = params$fastq_r1,
  fastq.read2       = params$fastq_r2,
  barcodes.genes    = params$barcodes_genes,
  set.names         = params$set_names,
  set.sizes         = as.integer(params$set_sizes),
  # the same list twice, on purpose: as the whitelist it error-corrects the
  # barcode; as called.cells it fixes the denominator of the final panels
  cell.whitelist    = file.path(SCRATCH, params$cell_whitelist),
  called.cells      = file.path(SCRATCH, params$cell_whitelist),
  output_dir        = OUT,
  sample_name       = params$sample_name,
  percentage        = params$percentage,
  ratio             = params$ratio,
  UMI.count         = params$umi_count,
  min.cell.UMI      = params$min_cell_umi,
  max.edit.distance = params$max_edit_distance,
  jitter            = params$jitter,
  max.reads         = MAXR,
  verbose           = FALSE)
# The entry point nests its outputs one level down, under the chemistry name,
# so another pipeline writing into the same Output/ cannot overwrite these.
# Take the path from the object rather than rebuilding it here.
OUT <- res$output_dir
res
```

## Where the reads went

```{r read-classes}
kable(res$read_class, caption = "Read fates")
```

```{r funnel, fig.cap="Read fates, each stage a subset of the one above"}
show("tenxcatch_detection_funnel", "png")
```

## Construct geometry as the data confirms it

Read 1 is `[cell barcode 16][UMI 12] …` at fixed offsets — the same slice the
original shell pipeline cut with `cut -c 1-16` and `cut -c 17-28`. Read 2
carries the cassette as `rc(reference) rc(UCI) rc(barcode) constant …`, and
those fields are read relative to the **vector constant**, not to the
reference, so a read carrying a sequencing error inside the reference anchor is
still recovered with the right barcode.

```{r geometry}
p <- res$params
kable(data.frame(
  field = c("reference", "empty reference", "vector constant", "UCI length",
            "barcode length", "cell barcode length", "UMI length",
            "barcode correction radius"),
  value = c(p$reference, p$empty.reference, p$constant, p$UCI.length,
            p$barcode.length, p$cb.length, p$umi.length, p$max.edit.distance)))
```

## Which barcodes are cells

The knee separates real cells from the ambient floor. On 10x the whitelist *is*
Cell Ranger's called-cell list, so the two agree by construction — the panel is
still worth reading for where the knee falls relative to the UMI floor.

```{r rank, fig.cap="Barcode-rank curve against the called-cell count"}
show("tenxcatch_barcode_rank", "png")
```

## Would more sequencing help?

Answered by subsampling the reads supporting each molecule, not by extrapolating
a fitted curve past the data.

```{r saturation, fig.cap="Rarefaction and marginal return"}
show("tenxcatch_saturation", "png")
```

## Threshold suggestions

```{r thresholds}
thr <- res$thresholds
kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("(cell, UCI) pairs", "single-UMI pairs", "% single-UMI",
               'mode = "noise" would pick', 'mode = "bimodal" would pick',
               "applied (UMI.count)", "applied (min.cell.UMI)"),
  value = c(thr$pairs, thr$singletons, round(thr$pct_singletons, 1),
            thr$noise, thr$bimodal, params$umi_count, params$min_cell_umi)),
  caption = "Threshold estimators (NA = the estimator found nothing to cut on)")
```

```{r diag, fig.cap="Call accuracy and the percentage sweep"}
show("tenxcatch_call_accuracy", "png"); show("tenxcatch_threshold_sweep", "png")
```

# The thirteen catcheR plots

Written under catcheR's own file names, as `.jpg` and `.pdf`, so a 10x figure
from this pipeline can be dropped in beside one from the original.

```{r plots-1}
for (f in c("barcode_distribution", "gene_distribution", "UMIxUCI", "UCIxcell",
            "percentage_of_UMIxUCI_dist", "2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count")) show(f)
```

# Cell filtering

```{r filter}
flt <- catcheR_tenx_filtercatch(res,
  # the files a later step reads are copied into scratch/, renamed with the
  # chemistry and the sample, so several pipelines can share one scratch
  to.scratch   = if (isTRUE(params$to_scratch)) SCRATCH else NULL,
  UMI.count = params$umi_count, percentage = params$percentage,
  ratio = params$ratio, min.cell.UMI = params$min_cell_umi,
  output_dir = OUT, jitter = params$jitter, verbose = FALSE)
kable(flt$filter_returns, caption = "What the filter returns at each threshold")
```

```{r plots-2}
show("2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_thresholds"); show("true_UCIxcell")
show("cellsxclone"); show("2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_ValidCells")
```

# Unperturbed cells

```{r nocatch}
noc <- catcheR_tenx_nocatch(res, filtered = flt, verbose = FALSE)
```

# Join to the expression matrix

Optional, and skipped automatically when the Cell Ranger files are not in
`scratch/`. Cell Ranger writes `barcodes.tsv.gz` as the 16 nt barcode with a
`-1` suffix; the suffix is stripped on both sides, so the join is a plain
string match.

```{r seurat}
gex <- file.path(SCRATCH, c("matrix.mtx.gz", "features.tsv.gz", "barcodes.tsv.gz"))
if (all(file.exists(gex))) {
  obj <- catcheR_tenx_seurat(res, filtered = flt, empty = noc,
                             mtx = gex[1], features = gex[2], cells = gex[3],
                             sample_id = params$sample_name,
                             project = params$sample_name,
                             rename = TRUE, subset.valid = TRUE,
                             output_dir = OUT, verbose = TRUE)
} else {
  message("Cell Ranger matrix not found in scratch/ - skipping the join.")
}
```

When you scale this to several samples, attach the metadata to each object
*before* `merge(..., add.cell.ids = ...)`. The merge prefixes every barcode
with the sample id, after which the 16 nt key no longer matches.
